`absent` is reachable BEFORE ledger publication and after a fail-soft
ledger-write failure: a healthy append can be absent from HEAD and transiently
absent from the worktree while no ledger row exists yet, and section 4.1 plus
P1/P3/P4 make that single snapshot actionable. Remedy: synchronize
classification with the writer so durable in-flight evidence exists before the
revertible append interval; any failure to establish or read that evidence must
produce a typed non-actionable `unknown` / `error`, NEVER `absent`. Codex notes

MF-3 (Codex methodology) — NOT raised by any other lens, and the cheapest of
the three to fix.
HEAD operational failures are collapsed into missing evidence. Section 4.1
treats a generic `git show` failure as a missing current path, falls back to the
registry, and eventually contributes `[]`. So a repository / process / read
failure — not path absence — can turn a COMMITTED marker into an actionable
`absent`, silently conflating rc 4 with infrastructure failure. Remedy: only a
VERIFIED missing-path result may enter the registry fallback or contribute `[]`;
operational git failures must return a typed non-actionable error with a generic
nonzero exit code, reserving rc 4 exclusively for a complete, successful
three-source read. Tests: inject non-path `git show` failures independently on
the direct-path and registry legs with worktree and ledger empty; assert
error / generic-nonzero and never `absent` / rc 4.

Unified design implication for v2: `absent` must require POSITIVE evidence that
all three legs were read successfully and completely, and the helper needs a
fourth typed verdict (`unknown` / `error`) for any incomplete or failed read.

So under the v2 predicate the probe reads LIVE essentially always, and
`absent` — the ONLY verdict that can support a missing-marker conclusion — is
reachable roughly 1 time in 10,000. §6 criterion 2 and the P1/P3/P4 escalation
guard both depend on `absent` being obtainable when a marker really is gone;
under v2 they are inert.

**Why v2's severity argument does not save it.** §4.1 classifies the constant as
ADVISORY-DIRECTION on the grounds that "a false positive withholds an actionable
`absent` for one ~60-90 s re-read cycle (safe direction), never licenses an
action", and therefore exempts it from a discriminating-band derivation. The
reasoning is sound but the premise is false: with a 32 s inter-arrival rate the
re-read NEVER clears, so the withholding is permanent, not one cycle. A gate
whose satisfying condition is essentially never attainable is the
unreachable-rejection-region class — see
`.claude/rules/selection-symmetric-nulls.md` § "Gate thresholds on a NULL
statistic need a MEASURED calibration basis" and § "Band-vs-ceiling
informativeness check". The severity class was right; the missing step was
measuring the distribution the constant is pinned against.

**The fix — scope the signal to windows that are actually live.** Two
measurements point the same way:

1. **Pid-liveness is perfectly discriminating right now.** The patch filename is
   `patch{epoch}-{pid}` (`staged_files_only.py:68`), so the owning pid is free
   to read. Measured: of the 4 files fresher than 300 s, **0** have a live
   `/proc/<pid>`; of the 12 fresher than 900 s, **0**. Every fresh patch file on
   this box belongs to a finished commit — i.e. a CLOSED window. A dead pid's
   patch file is not a live stash window at any mtime.
2. **A stash window in ANOTHER repo cannot revert THIS repo's files.**
   pre-commit's `git checkout -- .` is scoped to the repo being committed, so a
   global-directory signal imports cross-repo noise with no corresponding
   signal. The owning pid's `/proc/<pid>/cwd` resolves inside the repo it is
   committing, which makes repo-scoping cheap and read-only.

Land a predicate along those lines: signal 2 fires only for a patch file whose
embedded pid is STILL ALIVE **and** whose `/proc/<pid>/cwd` resolves inside this
repo, with the mtime bound kept as a cheap secondary guard against pid recycling
(a recycled pid plus a stale mtime is then harmless). Keep signal 1
(`index.lock` in THIS repo) as-is — it is already correctly repo-scoped, and it
is the leg that covers the deferral-in-progress case.

Note the composition you must preserve: signal 1 may NOT cover the whole hook
window (`git checkout -- .` takes the index lock only briefly, while the hook
suite runs afterward), which is presumably why signal 2 exists. So signal 2 is
genuinely needed — it just has to be scoped to this repo and to live pids rather
than to global mtime freshness.

**State the reachability.** Whatever predicate you land, the plan must state the
MEASURED reachability of `absent` under it — the same measurement shape above,
re-run against the final predicate — so the next reviewer does not have to
re-derive it. If a residual unreachability remains, name it in §12 with its
measured probability rather than an adjectival claim.

**Test it.** T1 case 4 already monkeypatches `PRE_COMMIT_HOME` to a per-test tmp
dir, which is the right determinism lever — extend it so the suite proves BOTH
directions: a dead-pid fresh patch file must NOT block `absent`, and a live-pid
in-repo patch file (or a present `index.lock`) MUST force `unknown`. Without the
dead-pid case the suite cannot distinguish the v2 predicate from the fixed one.
